summary: The starter prompt is actionable: it clearly specifies a Node.js LangChain orchestration that queries DocumentDB for carts abandoned >2 hours, generates personalized copy, routes via a channel agent (email/SMS), and logs outcomes back to DocumentDB. Several implementation details (driver version, exact schema, model/provider credentials, delivery provider, run surface, seed-script & tests, README conventions) are not specified and will be filled by the builder using the provided skill guidance or reasonable defaults.

rubric.found_in_prompt: “build a Node.js LangChain orchestration pipeline that queries DocumentDB for carts abandoned for over 2 hours, passes each cart to a copy-generation agent ... then ... channel agent ... Log outcomes back to DocumentDB.”
rubric.note: Business problem, user (retail recovery), and what to demonstrate are clearly stated.

rubric.found_in_prompt: “Node.js LangChain orchestration pipeline ... copy-generation agent ... channel agent”
rubric.note: Multi-agent orchestration with LangChain is explicit.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt: “Node.js”. skill.md: “Node.js 24 with npm and npx is available.”
rubric.note: Node.js is required; run environment supplies Node.js 24.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt implies using a Node.js MongoDB driver but doesn't name a package or version.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will use the official `mongodb` npm package and pick a modern, Node-24-compatible release (e.g. mongodb 5.x) and follow the singleton-client pattern from documentdb-driver.
rubric.note: Best-practice guidance (singleton client, reuse) exists in documentdb-driver but no explicit package/version is mandated by the prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill.md: a vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol, DiskANN, HNSW and IVF vector indexes) is reachable; connection string in DOCUMENTDB_URI.
rubric.note: Run environment fixes the cluster and tier to use; builder must not provision another cluster.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill.md: “connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time. Never write its value into any file, log ... use a config file or `.env.example` with a placeholder.”
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Model/API provider credentials are not specified; builder will place provider keys (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY, TWILIO_API_KEY, SENDGRID_API_KEY) in env vars and document them in .env.example.
rubric.note: DB secret location is specified; AI/model provider secrets are not mentioned and must be added by the implementer.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt references carts and a customer's stored preference (email/SMS) but gives no schema.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create collections such as `carts` (fields: _id, customerId, items[], lastActivity: Date, total), `customers` (customerId, name, email, phone, channelPreference), and `recovery_logs` or update-cart fields for outcome. Use embedding of cart items and minimal cross-collection lookups.
rubric.note: The modeling skill gives patterns and rules to design the schema; concrete field names/types will be chosen by the builder.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt asks to query for abandoned carts but does not describe sample data or seeding.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will supply a small synthetic seed script that inserts a few customers and carts (e.g. 5–20 carts) and can be run idempotently (upsert or check by unique test marker).
rubric.note: skill.md instructs to 'create the collections and indexes, load the sample data' during verification, but source/size/license and an idempotent seed script are not provided.

rubric.found_in_prompt: “queries DocumentDB for carts abandoned for over 2 hours” (implies a $lt on last-activity timestamp).
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will implement a find/aggregation with { lastActivity: { $lt: new Date(Date.now() - 2*60*60*1000) } } and create an index on lastActivity (and likely customerId) to make the query efficient; optionally a TTL index or a separate `status` field/index can be added for lifecycle.
rubric.note: Query-generation guidance and index-design practices are available via skills; the prompt doesn't enumerate indexes explicitly.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt requires a LangChain copy-generation agent and a channel agent but does not name model(s), provider, or call locations.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will use a hosted LLM provider supported by LangChain (e.g. OpenAI) and expect credentials via env vars (OPENAI_API_KEY). The copy agent will call the chat/completion model to produce personalized messages; no embeddings are strictly required for simple copy generation.
rubric.note: Model choice, model name, rate limits, and where in the code to call models must be decided by the implementer and documented in .env.example/README.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt asks for a Node.js LangChain orchestration pipeline but does not specify whether it is a CLI script, scheduled job (cron), serverless function, or HTTP API.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will implement a simple CLI/Node script (npm run start) that runs the pipeline once per invocation and document how to schedule it (cron/azure function) in the README. It may also expose a small HTTP endpoint for manual runs if convenient.
rubric.note: App surface affects how MongoClient is initialized (long-running server vs one-shot script) and connection pool tuning; documentdb-connection skill provides guidance.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill.md: “This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned ... Do not provision another cluster unless the run policy says Azure writes are allowed; the cluster above is the one to use.”
rubric.note: Deployment/provisioning of DocumentDB is not required and should not be attempted by the sample; infrastructure-as-code for cluster is not expected in this sample run.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt requests the sample but contains no explicit run commands or test instructions.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will add README commands: npm install, npm run seed, npm start (or node src/run.js), and include simple unit tests (jest) that mock the MongoDB client and LangChain calls so tests run without a live cluster.
rubric.note: skill.md asks the builder to verify against the live cluster, but explicit developer-facing run/test steps must be added to the repo.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt defines the flow but does not give explicit acceptance criteria.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will treat 'done' as: sample loads seed data; pipeline finds carts >2h old; copy agent generates messages; channel agent sends (or simulates send) via distinct email/SMS code paths; each attempt is logged to DocumentDB; README documents how to run and verify.
rubric.note: Add concrete checks in README and scripts (e.g. sample query results, log documents) as acceptance criteria.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill.md: run against existing live cluster; do not run a local DocumentDB gateway; do not write connection strings to files; use database `sample_retail_12`.
rubric.note: skill.md imposes useful constraints (use live cluster, DB name). The builder should follow these non-goals (no provisioning, no leaking secrets).

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt does not specify folder layout, README structure, .env.example contents, or dependency pinning conventions.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will use a conventional Node repo layout (src/, tests/, scripts/), include a README with sections (what it shows, prerequisites, setup, run, clean-up), provide a `.env.example` with placeholders (DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY, TWILIO_* or SENDGRID_*), and include package-lock.json to pin dependencies.
rubric.note: These repo conventions are required for gallery samples but must be added by the implementer; some guidance exists in documentdb-local-deployment about env-driven config.

questions_for_author: Which LLM provider and model should the copy-generation agent use (e.g. OpenAI gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, Anthropic, or a stub)?

Should the sample actually send real emails/SMS, and if so which delivery providers are preferred (SendGrid/SMTP for email, Twilio for SMS)? Or should these be implemented as mockable adapters and documented how to wire real credentials?
What app surface do you prefer for the sample: a one-shot CLI/script (invoked by cron), an HTTP endpoint, or a serverless function? (This affects connection pooling defaults.)
Do you require an idempotent seed script and a small deterministic dataset included in the repo, or is a script that generates synthetic test data acceptable?
requirements_at_risk: A `.env.example` that lists every setting with placeholder values — prompt/skills mention some env vars (DOCUMENTDB_URI) but do not require a complete .env.example for model and delivery provider keys.

Vector index dimensions and parameter tuning for the embedding model — the prompt does not use embeddings explicitly; vector-index requirements from the reference are likely irrelevant or will be omitted.
Seed script that can be run twice without duplicating data — prompt/skill.md instruct loading sample data but no explicit idempotency rule or implementation is given.

Search-related behaviour (e.g. /search error messages on empty query or embedding failure, similarity scores) — this sample doesn't explicitly implement a search endpoint, so those reference requirements are at risk.
Unit tests that run without a live cluster — nothing in the prompt mandates test harnesses or mocks; builder must add them explicitly.

Dependencies pinned in a requirements file — for Node, package-lock.json will pin deps but the reference mentioned `requirements.txt`; the prompt doesn't state how to pin or which lockfile to include.
Infrastructure-as-code for the cluster — skill.md states a cluster already exists and that the sample should not provision another cluster, so repo will likely not include Azure infra code.
